note: MLE key is set from the default master key (00 11 22 33 44 55 66 77 88 99 aa bb cc dd ee ff) via HMAC-SHA256, enabling decryption of the attacker-controlled MLE message.
MLE header indicates IEEE 802.15.4 security; the message is decrypted and validated, then the command is dispatched.
MLE command is kCommandParentResponse (10), so HandleParentResponse is called.
The Response TLV is parsed from the attacker-controlled message. The TLV length is set to 255, which passes IsValid() because it only checks GetLength() >= 8.
IsValid() returns true for length 255 because there is no upper-bound check; sizeof(*this)-sizeof(Tlv) = 8, and 255 >= 8.
memcmp reads response.GetLength() (255) bytes from the 8-byte mResponse[8] stack buffer, causing a stack-buffer-overflow READ.
